headline: Stock slide and PBOC cash end a four-day sell-off; CGB 10Y back to 1.606%, CDB spread in to 8.7bp
summary: Monday's tax-day sell-off took the CCDC 10-year to 1.628% (+1.6bp) and the 30-year to 2.082%, but Tuesday reversed it: the 10-year fell 2.3bp to 1.606% and the 30-year 2.5bp to 2.057%, with the 50-year (−3.3bp) and the 5-year (−2.3bp) leading while the 2-year eased 1.0bp to 1.230%. Policy banks outperformed after last week's tax repricing: CDB 10-year fell 3.7bp to 1.693%, cutting its spread over CGB to 8.7bp from 10.2bp on Monday and 11.0bp on Friday, while CDB and ADBC 5-year fell 3.7–3.9bp and ADBC and EXIM 10-year 3.2bp.
drivers: Fund selling pauses; policy banks bounce hardest

CDB 3–10Y yields fell 3.1–3.7bp versus 1.8–2.3bp for CGBs, after the CDB 7-year spread over CGB touched 20.9bp on Monday. CITIC argues that any end to the tax exemption would spare existing bonds and flags 7–10Y CDB as value; ADBC's 7-year tap cleared at 1.621% with 3.6 times cover. Brokers still say fund redemptions have not clearly eased, so swings stay wide.
October activity misses across the board

Industrial output grew 4.8% (f 5.3%), retail sales 0.4% (f 0.8%) and fixed investment fell 8.1% year-to-date (f −7.0%), with property investment down 21.6%. Bonds ignored it on Monday amid tax-day funding and redemptions, but it reinforces the weak-demand case once selling fades.
Tax-day funding firm, PBOC adds overnight cash

DR001 rose to about 1.30% and DR007 to 1.396% on Monday, a one-month high. The PBOC added a net RMB96bn of overnight reverse repos at 1.25% on Monday and RMB254bn on Tuesday, but rolled the 6-month outright repo RMB100bn short, leaving November's outright operations RMB300bn net drained.
Equities fall, helping the long end

The STAR index fell 5.4% and the Shanghai Composite 0.9% on Monday, with another drop of about 0.5% on Tuesday. Convertibles lost 3.2% on Monday, hurting fixed-income-plus funds, but on Tuesday the stock-bond seesaw worked: 30-year futures rose 0.88% and 10-year futures 0.21%.
data: Industrial output 4.8% y/y (f 5.3%, p 5.5%); retail sales 0.4% (f 0.8%, p 1.1%); FAI YTD −8.1% (f −7.0%, p −7.2%); property investment −21.6%
Broad miss with collapsing investment supports lower yields and the case for more fiscal and monetary support.
Smallest annual fall in 11 months but monthly declines persist, so no lift to credit demand yet.
New loans −RMB100bn (f +RMB20bn, p +RMB1.08tn); TSF RMB1.15tn (f 1.42tn, p 3.55tn); M2 7.1% (f 7.2–7.3%, p 7.2%); M1 4.4% (p 3.2%)
Record-low 4.7% loan growth confirms weak private demand and supports lower yields.
Strong external demand trims the growth-scare case for bonds and triggered mild profit-taking.
Soft household demand keeps the easing bias intact and supports low long-end yields.
Energy-driven cost push that squeezes margins rather than signalling demand; bonds looked through it.
Mfg 49.3 (f 50.0, p 50.1); new orders 49.4; non-mfg 49.7 (p 50.2); composite 49.7
Back in contraction with softer prices, which supports low yields and continued easy funding.
view: Mildly bullish for the next 1–2 weeks, with the 10-year expected in a 1.57–1.63% CCDC range. Monday's close at 1.628% filled my 10-year buy, and Tuesday's bounce plus a broad October activity miss support holding it toward 1.58%; the 5Y-into-10Y flattener stays on. Policy bank spreads have started to retrace, so I keep buyers' levels rather than chase: CDB 10Y at 12bp over CGB and CDB 7Y at 23bp after the 7Y trade was stopped on Monday. A formal plan to tax bond interest on existing holdings, another redemption wave in credit and wealth products, or DR001 holding above 1.35% would push the 10-year back through 1.64%; a 7-year special CGB auction that clears well on Wednesday and an LPR that hints at easing would speed the move to 1.58%.

buckets.name: CGB 1–2Y
buckets.why: The 2-year fell 1.0bp to 1.230% after touching 1.241% on Monday, still near its 1-year low (7th percentile, average 1.302%), and the 1-year is 1.171%. DR001 near 1.30% and a 6-month outright repo drain cap the front end even as the PBOC adds overnight cash.
buckets.call: Hold; add 2-year CGBs only above 1.27%, or if DR001 settles back toward 1.25%.

buckets.name: CGB 5–7Y belly
buckets.why: 2s5s10s is −16.5bp (8th percentile, average −8.0bp), so the 5-year at 1.335% stays rich, and 5s7s10s is −6.4bp (15th percentile) ahead of Wednesday's RMB150bn 7-year special CGB. The 5s10s flattener opened at ~29bp is at 27.0bp (46th percentile, average 26.6bp), still open and 2bp in the money.
buckets.call: Keep the 5Y-into-10Y switch (5s10s flattener) from ~29bp, target 25bp, stop 31bp.

buckets.name: CGB 10Y
buckets.why: Entry filled: the 10-year closed Monday at 1.628%, inside the 1.62–1.63% buy zone, and fell 2.3bp on Tuesday to 1.606% (2nd percentile, average 1.754%). Against neighbours it still screens cheap: 7s10s20s is −27.1bp (71st percentile, average −29.5bp), and the October activity miss strengthens the fundamental case.

buckets.name: CGB 30Y
buckets.why: The 30-year rose to 2.082% on Monday, short of the 2.10% add level, then fell 2.5bp to 2.057% as TL futures rallied 0.88%. 10s30s is 45.2bp (38th percentile, average 46.0bp) and 30s50s 11.0bp (4th percentile), so the long end is fairly priced against the 10-year; insurer and year-end demand should cap it.
buckets.call: Neutral. Add above 2.10% (10s30s ~46bp); poor risk/reward below 2.03%.

buckets.name: Policy banks 2–10Y vs CGB
buckets.why: The CDB 10-year spread over CGB peaked at 11.0bp on Friday, eased to 10.2bp on Monday and to 8.7bp on Tuesday (56th percentile, average 9.7bp), so the 12bp entry never traded. At 2Y policy banks remain tight (CDB 11.9bp, 3rd percentile), so value, if any, is at 7–10Y rather than the front.
buckets.call: Buy CDB 10Y vs CGB 10Y at 12bp or wider, target 9bp, stop 15bp; avoid 1–3Y policy banks.

buckets.name: Policy banks 5–7Y vs CGB
buckets.why: Stopped out: the CDB 7-year spread over CGB closed Monday at 20.9bp, above the 20.5bp stop, then narrowed 1.2bp on Tuesday to 19.7bp (74th percentile, average 15.8bp). ADBC 7Y is 19.1bp over CGB (98th percentile) and ADBC 5Y 16.7bp (80th), so the tax repricing is still embedded and the tenor is cheap, but I want a wider entry while redemptions continue.
buckets.call: Flat after the stop at ~20.9bp; re-enter CDB 7Y vs CGB 7Y at 23bp+, target 18bp, stop 26bp.

buckets.name: ADBC/EXIM vs CDB 10Y
buckets.why: ADBC 10-year yields 1.9bp more than CDB (59th percentile, average 1.4bp) after CDB led Tuesday's rally, and EXIM only 1.0bp (10th percentile, average 2.0bp). ADBC's pickup widened back from Friday's 1.4bp, and its auctions drew 3.6–4.9 times cover, so demand is intact.
buckets.call: Hold ADBC 10Y over CDB 10Y; switch back to CDB if the pickup falls below 1bp. Avoid EXIM 10Y at about 1bp.

buckets.name: Policy banks 20–30Y
buckets.why: The CDB 20-year spread over CGB is 9.8bp (53rd percentile, average 10.3bp) after both curves fell 2.0bp on Tuesday, near where I closed the CGB-over-CDB 20Y trade at ~9.5bp. The CDB 30-year spread is 11.0bp, its 1-year tight (0th percentile, average 12.5bp), so there is no value in long policy banks.
buckets.call: Flat; re-enter CGB 20Y over CDB 20Y below 7bp; avoid CDB 30Y at an 11bp spread.

watch: Next: the RMB150bn 7-year special CGB auction (Nov 18), APEC in Shenzhen (Nov 18–19), the LPR and a 30-year CGB reopening (Nov 20), October industrial profits (Nov 27), daily PBOC overnight operations at 1.25% and whether DR001 settles back below 1.30%, any official word on bond interest tax, fund redemption data, and US Treasury yields with markets pricing a December Fed hike.
